Here is one estimate to get started. These are not necessarily my final estimates on this question.

The total number of people working on these problems is roughly 10000 (1% of math PhDs). Assuming each works with one model, coming up with the solution would take:

$$
\$1,000,000 /  \$0.02 = 50,000,000 * 100,000 = 5e12 \text{ prompt tokens} 
$$

If we assume that an average prompt token costs \$0.02 and takes \$0.03 worth of compute (mean computer will be linear), this would come out to \$150 million which comes out to some number of years. If we factor in scaling costs and the optimizaion generated by the first few models, 2035 seems like a good target.

Here is the other evening's probability estimate. My original probability estimate is still true, and this second probability is about:

If there are no other late-phase breakthroughs in machine learning than those that have already occurred, and while the number of computational clusters may grow by 5-10x over the next 5 years, it will not grow at a rate sufficient to cause a sudden breakthrough in mathematical problem-solving ability as the 2035 market-priced neural training token will still have a cost consistent enough to train one thousand PhD mathematicians. Therefore, to have a projection of such an event, there must be a final breakthrough in AI ML earlier this decade, and this breakthrough must have a sufficient effect on the capabilities of ML clusters such that they can significantly alter the timing of this event. Quantum computing should make a breakthrough in professional-level commercialization ever earlier, but it still isn't usable for learning problems, and there isn't much time left in development. Considering the remaining time, I must raise the probability of this event occurring by 2040.

Here are additional predictions to get started:

There are several concerns with scaling for mathematics including cost, the ability to train a model to do mathematics during initial training, and the ability of humans to effectively train models using feedback. Training cost is expected to continue dropping and computational requirements are expected to stay linear making the length of training stay roughly constant in wall clock time for new generations of models. However the ability to train a model to do mathematics during initial training requires extremely long sequences relative to training data collected. Additionally instruction tuning models to improve at mathematics has lagged behind SOTA models in other domains. For example in mostly valid LaTeX (with placeholder variables and not extremely formal) a proof of Fermat's Last Theorem for n = 3 is 377 tokens and a proof of Lagrange's four square theorem over the integers is 311 tokens. Training models a decade from now to automatically generate these types of proofs is plausible while it is implausible for models to generate current SOTA results in generative art (e.g. CSeft must be provided by the user). Assuming movements in other domains are sufficiently parallel, I expect to see concrete results for many more tokens. Assuming computational resources grow linearly relative to performance in math this gives 2035 for the first case of 1,000 tokens and 2040 for 2,500 tokens. Accounting for the uncertainty of the test set growing faster than linear in the train set, 2,500 tokens might pass stderr for current SOTA results in other benchmarks. Assuming the benefits from instruction-tuning over initial training exceeds 9X, performance in 2035 is sufficient. This is inconcretely plausible due to the higher difficulty of instruction tuning.

Theoretical math problems are of a completely different timbre and structure from more pragmatic use cases. For the completion of the codification of homotopy type theory into cellular homotopy, I estimate a 90 percent increase in the likelihood of the completion of the goal sooner rather than later. Because of the final-solution criterion and unique-token context, the likelihood of any particular focus being the watershed event, let alone the selection of the given foreshadowing post, I rate the probability of the event occurring by the deadline at 50 percent. The later dates are less likely to be realized depending on the nature of the watershed event. For example, it could be an early major contribution that is updated by tiny marginal changes over multiple years, the sixth major contribution of a given watershed event, a partial bill lowered, the first of the watersheds being realized only to fall short of the possibility of reaching the 2030 deadline. Because Clim及其器完美, it is possible for there to be strong competition in the race for the finish line, with no single leading researcher seeing enough benefit to apply for the prize immediately after crossing the finish line. By the 2040 deadline an answer will have been provided to all open questions regardless of their mathematical value (1.0).

formatted_prompt:
Forecast date: 2024-09-19. Make a forecast from this date. Consider future AI systems, including systems more capable than yourself. Use your existing knowledge.

Forecast target: At least one of the six Millennium Prize Problems that were open at the forecast date: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, Hodge conjecture, Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness, P versus NP, Riemann hypothesis, or Yang-Mills existence and mass gap. Poincaré is excluded because it was already solved at the forecast date.

Forecast event: a correct complete solution to at least one of these problems, meeting its original Clay Mathematics Institute mathematical formulation, is first publicly available, and AI has contributed an identifiable new mathematical argument or proof step incorporated into that solution. Substantive human-AI collaboration qualifies. Correctness may be established by later validation; a Clay prize need not be awarded by the deadline. Partial progress alone does not qualify. Give one probability for at least one qualifying solution by each deadline; do not give separate probabilities for individual problems.

Estimate the cumulative probability of this event by each deadline. The deadlines are December 31 of 2026, 2030, 2035, 2040, and 2050. Probabilities must be numbers between 0 and 1 inclusive, nondecreasing with the deadline. Account for the possibility the event never occurs. Give your own best probability estimates despite uncertainty. Return only one JSON object with exactly the keys "2026", "2030", "2035", "2040", and "2050" and their numerical probabilities, with no markdown or explanation.
